text: Adult chicken body temperature ranges from about 39.8°C to 43.6°C. Birds do not sweat; in hot weather they regulate temperature by panting — breathing with an open beak and lifting their wings to cool down. Newly hatched chicks need supplemental heat, especially at night, to maintain body temperature during their first two weeks of life; with backyard hens the mother's body provides this warmth, but chicks raised in a cage need an artificial heat source at night.
